content.text: Public transit is more than a mode of transport — it is a thread that connects people to jobs, healthcare, education, and social networks. In post-industrial cities, the shape of that thread determines who can participate in the urban economy and who is left behind.

My ongoing research in Chicago examines how transit accessibility correlates with job access and health outcomes across different neighborhoods. Early findings suggest that areas with frequent, reliable service see significantly better economic mobility outcomes, even when controlling for income and education levels.

Consider two neighborhoods just three miles apart: one with a rail station and frequent bus service, the other with a single bus line that runs every `45 minutes`. Residents in the first neighborhood can reach **200,000 jobs * https://example.com** within a 45-minute commute. In the second, that number drops to 15,000.
Transit is the thread that connects people to opportunity. When that thread frays, entire communities are left behind.
content.source: Dr. Sarah Chen, Transit Equity Study (2026)

Residents in high-frequency transit corridors enjoy access to hundreds of thousands of jobs, while those in low-frequency areas are effectively cut off from economic opportunity. This is not merely a convenience issue - it is a structural barrier to social mobility.
A new rail line without rent stabilization risks pricing out the very communities it was meant to serve.

content.text: Without anti-displacement measures, new transit infrastructure can accelerate gentrification and harm the communities it aims to serve.

To replicate the analysis, use the `transit_equity` Python package. The core function `calculate_access()` takes a GTFS feed and census tract boundaries as input. Run the analysis with the `--mode transit` flag.

content.code:
import transit_equity as te

feed = te.load_gtfs("chicago_transit.zip")
tracts = te.load_census_tracts("cook_county.geojson")

results = te.calculate_access(
    feed=feed,
    tracts=tracts,
    commute_time=45,
    mode="transit"
)
print(results.head())
